svg.title: Decision tree: which way to shrink a GIF first
svg.desc: Start with trimming if the GIF is longer than needed, then resizing if it is shown smaller than its pixel size, then dropping frames if it has more frames than the motion needs, and finally compression with lossy settings and fewer colours. A strict size target goes to the compressor's target-size mode.
svg.text: Which fix first? Work down the questions.

g.text: 1. Longer than the moment you need?
Cut the start or end you do not need.
YES → Trim it
Shorter animation, same look
No ↓
2. Shown smaller than its pixel size?
Match the size it will actually display at.
YES → Resize it
Half the width = a quarter of pixels
No ↓
3. More frames than the motion needs?
Keep the duration, show fewer frames.
YES → Drop frames
Motion gets choppier — check it
No ↓
4. Still too big, or a strict size limit?
Optimize, then lossy and fewer colours.
YES → Compress it
Raise strength only until it fits
No ↓
Need an exact size? Use the compressor's target-size mode.
It tries stronger settings in passes and says honestly if the target cannot be reached.

svg.text: Free fixes first (trim, resize), visible trade-offs last (frames, colours, lossy).
